descriptionChirho: Physical or abstract strength, might, or power, whether of God, a person, or a nation; the dominant sense of the noun, rendered consistently as Arabic عِزّ/قُوَّة, Korean 힘/능력, and Swahili nguvu across all pronominal suffixes and prepositional prefixes.

A place of fortified refuge or stronghold, a metaphorical extension from abstract strength to a concrete defensive place; confirmed by Arabic حِصْنِهَا (her fortress) and Swahili ngome-yake (her fortress), distinct from the abstract noun.

Severity, harshness, or insolent boldness, as in the construct 'oz panim' (brazenness of face); distinguished from mere strength by Arabic قَسَاوَة (harshness), Hindi कठोरता (hardness), and Swahili ugumu (hardness/toughness).

Adjectival or attributive use describing something as fortified, secure, or impregnable (e.g., a fortified city); confirmed by Arabic حَصِين (impregnable), Hindi मज़बूत/दृढ़ (firm/strong), Korean 강한 (strong), and Swahili lenye-nguvu (having strength).
